tx.t: In this lecture I will describe the world's rainforests and why scientists want to protect them. Rainforests cover only about six per cent of the Earth's land surface.
However, they are home to more than half of all the plant and animal species on land. The Amazon is the largest rainforest, and it spreads across nine countries.
A rainforest has four main layers: the emergent layer, the canopy, the understorey and the forest floor. Most animals live in the canopy, where there is plenty of light and fruit.
Many modern medicines come from rainforest plants, and scientists believe thousands more are still unknown.

tx.t: Today I want to explain why sleep is so important, and what happens in the brain during the night. Adults need between seven and nine hours of sleep a night, while teenagers need eight to ten.

A full cycle of sleep lasts about ninety minutes, and we go through four or five cycles each night. Most vivid dreams happen during a stage called REM sleep, when the eyes move quickly under the eyelids.

While we sleep, the brain moves memories from short-term storage into long-term storage. Lack of sleep makes it harder to concentrate and slows reaction times, which is why tired drivers cause many accidents.
On average, people spend about one third of their lives asleep.

tx.t: I would like to tell you about the history of Fenwick. The town received its market charter in twelve forty-two, and it became known for its cloth.
In eighteen fifty-five, the population was about four thousand. Over the next fifty years it grew to twenty-eight thousand.
Then things changed, because the main road was moved outside the centre. As a result, fewer travellers passed through the market.

tx.t: In today's lecture, I will talk about the growth of cities. In two thousand and seven, for the first time in history, more than half of the world's people lived in cities.
The United Nations expects the figure to reach about two thirds by twenty fifty. Cities take up only about two per cent of the Earth's land, but they produce most of the world's wealth.
Rapid growth can cause housing shortages, traffic jams and air pollution. Some cities are planting trees and building cycle lanes to make urban life healthier.

tx.t: The new Redford library opened in twenty thirteen, at a cost of forty million pounds. It has six floors and holds more than one hundred and thirty-six thousand books.
Its most unusual feature is a recording studio, which is used mainly for young musicians.
The library is open ninety-seven hours a week, and membership is free for everyone who lives in the city.
